scenario.title: 看展、聊作品、表達感受
scenario.context: 描述展覽和作品時，英文常用分詞構句把兩個動作濃縮成一句：「走進展間，我第一眼就看到那幅畫」「用回收材料做成，這件作品…」。學會分詞構句，描述會更流暢、更像書寫的英文。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: So what did you think of the first room?
lines.zh: 你覺得第一個展間怎麼樣？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Honestly, I was blown away. Walking in, I didn't expect the whole ceiling to be covered in paper cranes.
lines.zh: 說真的我被震撼到了。一走進去，完全沒想到整個天花板都是紙鶴。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Me too. Made from old newspapers, the cranes tell the story of the city.
lines.zh: 我也是。那些紙鶴是用舊報紙做的，訴說著這座城市的故事。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: What about the video room? That one went a bit over my head.
lines.zh: 那錄像展間呢？那個我有點看不懂。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Same. Having read the description twice, I still don't get it.
lines.zh: 我也是。說明讀了兩遍還是不懂。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Video art isn't really my cup of tea. I prefer things I can touch.
lines.zh: 錄像藝術不太是我的菜，我比較喜歡摸得到的東西。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.zh: 真不愧是插畫家會說的話。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: This place is so artsy. Even the tote bags look like art pieces.
lines.zh: 這裡好文青，連帆布袋都像藝術品。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Designed by local artists, all of these are limited editions.
lines.zh: 這些都是本地藝術家設計的，全都是限量版。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Feeling inspired, I might start painting again.
lines.zh: 受到啟發，我可能會重新開始畫畫。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: You should! You were really good in college.
lines.zh: 你應該畫！你大學時畫得很好。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Not being very patient, I usually give up after a week.
lines.zh: 我沒什麼耐心，通常一個禮拜就放棄了。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Then start small. Buy this sketchbook and draw one thing a day.
lines.zh: 那就從小地方開始，買這本素描本，每天畫一樣東西。

patterns.en: I'm not sure I get it.
What's the artist trying to say?
It's not really my cup of tea.

chinglish.wrong: When I walk in, I saw the painting.
chinglish.right: Walking in, I saw the painting. / When I walked in, I saw the painting.
chinglish.why: 時態要一致；或者用分詞構句簡化。

chinglish.wrong: Made by recycled paper, the artwork is special.
chinglish.right: Made from recycled paper, the artwork is really unique.
chinglish.why: 看得出原料時 made of，原料已改變形態時 made from。special 也常被過度使用。

chinglish.wrong: Walking in the museum, the painting was beautiful.
chinglish.right: Walking through the museum, I saw a beautiful painting.
chinglish.why: 分詞構句的主詞要跟主要子句相同。原句變成「畫在走路」，是很經典的錯誤（dangling participle）。

chinglish.wrong: This exhibition is very high level.
chinglish.right: This exhibition is really sophisticated / impressive.
chinglish.why: 「很有水準」直翻 high level 不自然。

grammar.title: 分詞構句入門
grammar.oneLiner: 兩個子句主詞相同時，可以把其中一個濃縮成 V-ing（主動）或 p.p.（被動）開頭的片語。
whenToUse: 主動、同時發生：Walking in, I saw the cranes.（= When I walked in, …）
被動：Made from old newspapers, the cranes…（= The cranes were made from…）
先發生：Having read the description, I still didn't get it.（= After I had read…）
原因：Feeling inspired, I started painting.（= Because I felt inspired…）
否定：Not being patient, I gave up.
最重要的規則：分詞的主詞必須和主要子句的主詞相同。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文可以很自由地省略主詞：「走進去，看到一幅畫」「用舊報紙做成，很有意義」。英文的分詞構句也能省略主詞，但有一個嚴格條件：省略的主詞必須跟後面的主詞是同一個。台灣人最常犯的錯是 Walking in the museum, the painting was beautiful，意思變成「畫在博物館裡走路」。

examples.correct: Walking along the river, we saw a street performer.
examples.incorrect: Walking along the river, a street performer was singing.
examples.note: 我們在走路，主詞要是 we。

examples.correct: Painted in 1920, the portrait is now worth millions.
Having finished the tour, we went to the café.
Not knowing the way, I asked a guard.
Feeling tired, she sat down on a bench.

quiz.question: ___ the gallery, I noticed a huge sculpture.
___ in 1890, this building used to be a train station.
quiz.explanation: 建築物是被建造的，用 p.p.。

quiz.question: ___ finished the exhibition, we grabbed a coffee. (先完成)
Which is correct?
options: Looking at the painting, tears came to my eyes.
Looking at the painting, I started to cry.
Looked at the painting, I cried.
quiz.explanation: 分詞主詞要跟主要子句相同（I）。

quiz.question: ___ knowing the artist, I didn't understand the reference. (否定)

slang.meaning: 不是我的菜、不合我的口味
slang.usage: 委婉地表示不喜歡某種東西或活動，英式起源。

risk.note: 禮貌又常用，不會冒犯喜歡那樣東西的人。

examples.en: Opera isn't really my cup of tea.
It's well made, but it's not my cup of tea.
examples.zh: 做得很好，但不合我的口味。

slang.usage: I was blown away by… = 被…深深打動或驚訝。

examples.en: I was blown away by the view from the top.
The client was blown away by your designs.
examples.zh: 客戶被你的設計驚艷到了。

slang.usage: 形容人、地方、東西很有藝術氣息，有時帶點「故作藝術」的調侃。英式也說 arty。

risk.note: 看語氣可能是稱讚，也可能是在揶揄太做作。

examples.en: Huashan is full of artsy shops and cafés.
examples.zh: 華山都是文青小店和咖啡廳。

examples.en: The movie was a bit too artsy for me.
examples.zh: 那部電影對我來說有點太文藝了。

slang.usage: It went over my head. = 我沒聽懂／沒看懂（笑話、概念、作品）。

examples.en: The joke went right over my head.
examples.zh: 那個笑話我完全沒聽懂。

examples.en: Most of the lecture was over my head.
examples.zh: 那場演講大部分我都聽不懂。

review.question: The painting is gone from the wall. Someone ___ moved it to another room.
review.explanation: 複習第 46 單元：推測過去用 must have + p.p.。

review.question: If I ___ rich, I'd buy that painting.
review.explanation: 複習第 45 單元：type 2 用 were。

review.question: The audio guide doesn't ___ to be working.
review.explanation: 複習第 43 單元：doesn't seem to。

review.question: If we ___ early, we'll avoid the crowds.
review.explanation: 複習第 39 單元：type 1 if 子句用現在式。

review.question: The artist ___ work we saw is from Tainan.
Which is correct?
review.explanation: 複習第 15 單元：頻率副詞放一般動詞前。

review.question: Which is correct?
options: Walking in, the art was amazing.
Walking in, I was amazed by the art.
review.explanation: 分詞構句的主詞要一致。
